data.body:
CI FAILURE ROOT-CAUSED — Verified-1 on 2503/2504/2505 (2506 not yet voted). LLM-Review +1 on all three.
pytest FAILED identically on ubuntu py3.11, 3.12 AND 3.13 => deterministic, NOT a flake. Did not
recheck; read the run.

DEFECT 1 (mine, in 2503): tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py::
test_make_lint_rejects_live_vocabulary_through_guard builds a SYNTHETIC mini-repo in tmp, copies a
known subset of scripts/ into it, and runs 'make lint sources=src' there. My new
check_mcp_library_parity.py line in the lint target runs inside that synthetic repo, where the script
was never copied => 'python: can't open file .../check_mcp_library_parity.py' => lint dies before the
assertion under test. The test already stubs EVERY gate that runs ahead of the guard, each with a
comment naming the ticket that added it — an established house convention I had not met. Fixed in
that style with a stub + comment naming 8ce5.

ATTRIBUTION LESSON: the isolation-guard implementer reported this exact failure as 'pre-existing,
unrelated', having verified by stashing ITS OWN changes. Sound reasoning, wrong conclusion — it was
pre-existing relative to its change but INTRODUCED BY MINE earlier in the same worktree. Stash-based
attribution cannot see a change that predates yours in a shared tree.

DEFECT 2 (mine, in 2506) — SERIOUS USABILITY BUG IN MY OWN GUARD, found while fixing defect 1:
  pytest tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py            -> 48 passed
  pytest 'tests/unit/test_check_criteria_vocabulary.py::test_long_matching_line_is_truncated'
                                                                 -> COLLECTION BLOCKED, no tests ran
The reported site belongs to test_current_repository_vocabulary_is_clean, which IS correctly marked.
Cause: the scan is per-FILE but exemptions arrive per COLLECTED ITEM. A node-id selection that
excludes the marked test never absorbs its marker, so _Exemptions.files stays empty for that path and
excuses() declines to excuse a finding belonging to a test that is not even running.
'pytest <file>::<one_test>' is the most common developer action — failing it spuriously on any file
with a marked hazard elsewhere is exactly the 'reddens things on day one' outcome the ticket warned
gets a guard REVERTED rather than adopted.
Wrote the regression RED (uncollected-owner returns None) plus its control (collected unmarked owner
still fails, names the file); confirmed exactly one RED with the control passing; dispatched the fix.
Required behaviour: a finding may fail only when attributable to a test IN the collected selection
that lacks a valid marker; a finding whose enclosing test is not collected is out of scope, not
excused. Module-level-helper file-scope fallback, undecidable-never-fails, and item.iter_markers
resolution all preserved.

MY PROCESS GAP, RECORDED: I ran make lint + make typecheck + targeted tests locally but never the
full suite, which is what CI runs. Both defects were reachable locally. Pre-flight for the remaining
leaves must include a full 'make test' or at minimum the tests that exercise make lint in a synthetic
repo.

ADVISORY FROM THE LLM CODE REVIEW WORTH ACTING ON (2503, non-blocking, 5 findings):
 - parameter parity is enforced only for 'exact' correspondences, and the COMMITTED MANIFEST ALREADY
   CONTAINS AN UNFLAGGED REAL MISMATCH: ready_tickets (co_names). Real gap, not style.
 - _facade_function falls open: if the stub-recovery scan finds no defining module it silently
   returns the stub, so a harness-rebound facade would be measured instead of the shipped one.
Both go into the 2503 amend alongside the stub fix.
